newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador holds out asylum possibility to Peru rebels.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador holds out asylum possibility to Peru rebels.

text.p: Ecuadoran President Abdala Bucaram said on Thursday he was ready to grant asylum to Peruvian rebels holding almost 400 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

"We have stated clearly that if we can be of help, providing the Peruvian government asks for it, we would accede to that," Bucaram replied when asked by journalists whether Ecuador would give asylum to the Peruvian guerrillas.

Nevertheless, Bucaram said the asylum would not be political. "We cannot talk about political asylum when we see terrorism and political delinquency ... in any case that expression is misused," he said.
Bucaram did not elaborate, and it was not immediately clear what kind of asylum Ecuador would consider granting the rebels or whether there had been any request from Peru for such an offer.
The president spoke hours after his Foreign Minister Galo Leoro Franco said the government was considering the possibility of allowing rebels to enter Ecuador.
Bucaram underlined that his government would support Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori as he sought to deal with the crisis.
"We are totally open and will support what the Peruvian government does," he said.
Negotiations were currently under way in Lima between the rebels and Red Cross officials, but so far there have been no breakthroughs.

Bucaram's offer came against a backdrop of historical enmity between Ecuador and Peru, which are at odds over a frontier issue that took them to war in 1995. Due to the hostage drama, the two countries postponed a meeting scheduled for Friday in Brazil to look for a solution.
The heavily armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas captured the ambassador's residence on Tuesday, taking hostage some 400 people who were attending a cocktail party.

The rebels have threatened to kill their captives, including many high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and government officials, if the Peruvian government does not release up to 500 of their jailed comrades.
